newsitem.title: CAMBODIA: Camdodian co-premier escalates attacks on monarchy.
newsitem.headline: Camdodian co-premier escalates attacks on monarchy.

text.p: Cambodian co-Premier Hun Sen escalated his verbal offensive against the monarchy on Saturday, saying he no longer wanted to be King Norodom Sihanouk's honorary godson or carry a royal title.
"If the king releases a royal decree taking away the (royal title of) Samdech, I will be happier because I didn't ask for it," Hun Sen said in a televised speech.
He added that he no longer wanted to be the king's honorary godson -- a status he said was conferred on him in 1991 when Sihanouk visited him in Phom Penh.

Hun Sen has said he wanted to ban royal family members from politics unless they renounced their royal status. He also has warned that he would cancel coming elections if the king, who has hinted he may abdicate, quits the throne to enter politics.

Analysts believe Hun Sen's attacks are motivated by fear that the highly popular king might join with the co-premier's political rivals in local and national elections scheduled for this year and next.
Co-premiers Prince Norodom Ranariddh, who is the king's son, and Hun Sen have lurched to one dispute after another since forming an uneasy coalition following U.N.-sponsored elections in 1993.
Their parties are expected to oppose each other in the polls.
